text:
Moritz Seider is wearing more of Detroit than any defenseman should have to. The Red Wings' season has been defined by Dylan Larkin telling the club he would no longer play for them and being suspended without pay on Oct. 29, and Seider is the one left standing in front of the microphones. Yahoo Sports wrote that he sounds like a captain after the Vegas loss. He is playing over 26 minutes a night, and over his last ten games it has been closer to 27.

The production looks thin at first glance: ten points, all assists, no goals on 32 shots. That is mostly bad luck. His chances are the same as last season, and Detroit is scoring 2.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey rated him the third most valuable defenseman in the league in 2025-26, strong at both ends, and nothing in this season's shot shares says that player has gone anywhere. Our projection has him adding around 57 points the rest of the way. The thing to watch is the workload: on a team this unsettled, 27 minutes can become 30, and trade pitches already name him alongside Larkin (Heavy.com floated a Boston package).
headline: Seider carries a team in turmoil
